root.name: Old Indian Defense: Normal Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 d6 3. Nc3 Nbd7 4. e4 e5 5. Nf3

overview: Black sets up a Philidor-like structure with ...d6, ...e5, ...Nbd7, ...Be7, ...c6 and castling, keeping the centre tense rather than fianchettoing. White gets a space edge with e4 and d4 and usually plays Be2, O-O and Re1, aiming at d5 or a central break. The game is solid and manoeuvring, with Black cramped but hard to break down.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Be2, O-O and Re1, then push d5 or exchange on e5 for a space edge.
Keep the centre tense and use extra space on the queenside with a4 or b4.

black_ideas.idea: Hold e5 with ...c6 and ...Be7, then play ...exd4 or ...Re8 and ...Bf8 for a solid game.
Wait for White to commit and break with ...exd4 or ...d5 when it is prepared.

typical_structures.structure: Black d6/e5 chain against White d4/e4, with tension in the centre (Philidor-style).

character.notes: Compact, hard-to-break-down structure; slow manoeuvring play.

soundness.notes: Sound; considered slightly passive, theory gives White a small edge.

structure.notes: Tension on d4/e5 is kept in the Ukrainian main line, so the centre is undecided.

approach.notes: Standard Indian line, used by King's Indian players to avoid the Samisch.

level.notes: Plans are clear; handling the cramped structure takes judgement.

character.reason: Philidor-like structure is cramped but hard to break down.

structure.reason: Centre tension left unresolved in the main line.

plans.reason: White's central space against Black's cramped set-up.
